title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: Student (EE1) shares their personal identity (student id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login and submission process. This act of sharing causes a threat because the portal can identify the student and potentially track their behavior or access patterns.

title: Student Data Processing at Destination
description: Upon receiving the submission (student id, work file, course, timestamp), the Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes this data. The destination element may store or use this information in a way that causes a threat, such as linking submissions to a specific student profile for analytics or access control.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF1) transmits meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., student ID, course ID, submission timestamp) in transit. This meta-data can be used to link or identify the student and the portal, enabling tracking or profiling even if the student's identity is not explicitly shared.

title: Identification of Student
description: The source element (P1) shares data containing a unique identifier (student id) for the requesting role. This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) because the data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, which can be used to link or identify the user.
assumptions: The data in the submission request includes a student id field.

title: Identification of Course
description: The source element (P1) shares data containing a unique identifier (course) for the requesting role. This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) because the data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (the course entity), which can be used to link or identify the user.
assumptions: The data in the submission request includes a course field.

title: Identification of File Reference
description: The source element (P1) shares data containing a unique identifier (file reference) for the requesting role. This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) because the data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (the file entity), which can be used to link or identify the user.
assumptions: The data in the submission request includes a file reference field.

title: Identification of Requesting Role
description: The source element (P1) shares data containing a unique identifier (requesting role) for the requesting role. This constitutes an Identifying threat (I) because the data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (the requesting role), which can be used to link or identify the user.
assumptions: The data in the submission request includes a requesting role field.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The assignment file (containing student id, course, and submission time) is explicitly shared from the Process (P2) to the DataStore (DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system transfers personal data across a boundary to a known third party (the store).
assumptions: The assignment file contains personal data (student id) that is being transferred.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: The assignment file is transmitted via the data flow (DF3) to the DataStore. The transmission itself exposes the data to potential interception or metadata-based identification, constituting a data-centric threat.
assumptions: The assignment file is transmitted over a network.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The DataStore (DS1) receives the assignment file and stores it. Storing the data constitutes a data disclosure as the system transfers the data to a known location for processing.
assumptions: The assignment file is stored in the DataStore.

title: Teacher's Request for Submission Queue
description: The teacher (ExternalEntity EE3) initiates a request to the Grades Portal Web App (Process P1) to retrieve the queue of submissions for their courses. This action triggers an Identifying threat (I.1.1) as the system processes the teacher's request to identify and retrieve specific data (the submission queue) for their courses.
assumptions: The teacher has access to the system and the system is configured to process requests for specific course submissions.

title: Grades Portal Web App Processes Teacher's Request
description: The Grades Portal Web App (Process P1) receives the teacher's request and processes it to retrieve the submission queue. This action triggers a Data threat (D.1.1) as the system processes the teacher's request to identify and retrieve specific data (the submission queue) for their courses.
assumptions: The system is configured to process requests for specific course submissions.

title: Student Data Exposure
description: The process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) shares student names, work content, and submission times with the external entity EE3 (Teacher). This interaction is valid under the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity), but the act of sharing sensitive student data with an external party introduces a privacy risk. The threat arises at the source element (S) because the process's act of sharing causes the exposure of the data.
assumptions: The portal is configured to share all submissions to the teacher.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow DF5 transmits student names, work content, and submission times between the portal and the teacher. The threat arises at the data flow (fl) because the data-centric threat involves meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them. The teacher's identity and the student's identity are linked via the data in transit, creating a potential for data-centric privacy threats.
assumptions: The portal and teacher exchange data via the standard web interface.

title: Teacher Data Processing
description: The destination element (EE3, Teacher) receives the student data and processes or stores it. The threat arises at the destination (D) because the teacher's act of receiving and processing student names, work content, and submission times may lead to unauthorized access, storage, or misuse of this sensitive information.
assumptions: The teacher's system is configured to store and process all submissions.

title: Teacher's Identity Disclosure
description: Teacher (EE3) shares their identity (grader id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to record a grade. This is a Low severity threat as the teacher's identity is disclosed to a system they are not authorized to access.

title: Teacher's Intent Disclosure
description: Teacher (EE3) shares their intent to record a grade (grade, feedback text) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1). This is an Invalid interaction (I) because the mapping table explicitly excludes ExternalEntity->Process interactions.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the teacher's grade and feedback text. The mapping table indicates this is a valid interaction (Process->Process), but the destination element (P1) may process or store this data in a way that causes a threat (e.g., storing sensitive student-teacher relationships without proper access controls).

title: Grade Record Exposure
description: The process P2 shares sensitive student and course data (student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, timestamp) with the data store DS2. This act of sharing causes a threat because the data is exposed to unauthorized access or processing without proper authorization controls.

title: Data Processing for Grading
description: The data store DS2 receives the grade record and processes it for grading purposes. This action causes a threat because the data is stored and potentially used for grading, which may involve sensitive student information.

title: Requesting Personal Data
description: The external entity (Student, EE1) requests its own personal data (grades and feedback) from the system. This action triggers an Identifying threat (I) because the system processes identified data, which can be used to identify the student and potentially infer sensitive information about their academic performance.
assumptions: The student has the right to access their grades and feedback.

title: Processing Personal Data
description: The process (Grades Portal Web App, P1) receives the student's request and processes the identified data (grades and feedback). This processing action can lead to a Data threat (D) if the system stores, uses, or discloses the data in a way that compromises privacy.
assumptions: The process follows standard security protocols.

title: Grade Data Exposure
description: The process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) shares its internal grade data with the external entity EE1 (Student). This interaction is valid under the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity), but the act of sharing sensitive internal data (grades) with an external party introduces a privacy risk. The threat arises at the source element (S) because the process's act of sharing causes the data to be exposed to the recipient.

title: Student Data Processing
description: The destination element (EE1, Student) receives the grades data. The context indicates this is a valid interaction (Process->ExternalEntity). However, the student entity is an external party, and the act of processing or storing the student's own grades in a system they do not control introduces a privacy risk. The threat arises at the destination element (D) because the recipient's processing actions cause the threat.

title: Identity Confusion
description: Parent (EE2) shares their identity with the system, which is then used to access the child's account. This creates a risk that the system cannot distinguish between the parent and the child, leading to unauthorized access to the child's data.
assumptions: The system treats the parent's login credentials as valid for the child's account.

title: Data Centric Threat: Identity Linking
description: The data flow transmits the parent's identity information (e.g., username, email, or session token) to the destination. This meta-data allows the system to link the parent's actions to the child's account, enabling the parent to access the child's private data.
assumptions: The system does not validate that the parent is the actual owner of the child's account.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The portal web app (P1) processes the parent's identity data to retrieve the child's grades. This processing action, without proper authorization or verification of the parent's identity, allows the system to access and potentially misuse the child's private educational data.
assumptions: The system has not implemented a mechanism to verify that the parent is the legitimate owner of the child's account.

title: Grade Data Exposure
description: The process P1 shares sensitive student grades with the external entity EE2. This interaction is valid (Process->ExternalEntity) but the act of sharing causes a threat because the destination (EE2) may process or store this data in a way that causes a privacy threat, such as storing it in a way that allows identification or linkage.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE2) is an external system that may not have appropriate controls for storing or processing this data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the parent entity has specific controls for storing this data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Data Linkage Risk
description: The data flow DF11 carries metadata about the parties involved (P1 and EE2). This metadata could be used to link or identify the student grades with other data held by the parent entity, potentially violating privacy.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE2) has access to the data flow metadata.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the parent entity has access to the data flow metadata.

title: Data Processing Risk
description: The destination entity (EE2) receives the grades and may process or store them in a way that causes a privacy threat, such as storing them in a way that allows identification or linkage.
assumptions: The parent entity (EE2) is an external system that may not have appropriate controls for storing or processing this data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the parent entity has specific controls for storing this data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Unauthorized Account Creation
description: ExternalEntity EE4 (School Administrator) creates accounts without proper authorization or verification, potentially allowing unauthorized users to access the system.
assumptions: No additional context provided to confirm the specific authorization process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific authorization process is fully documented in the context.

title: Inappropriate Account Modification
description: EE4 modifies account details (names, emails, roles) without verifying the user's identity or the legitimacy of the modification request.
assumptions: No additional context provided to confirm the specific verification process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific verification process is fully documented in the context.

title: Unauthorized Account Disabling
description: EE4 disables accounts without proper authorization or verification, potentially leaving the system in an inconsistent or insecure state.
assumptions: No additional context provided to confirm the specific authorization process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific authorization process is fully documented in the context.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: Process P1 processes account data (names, emails, roles) without proper validation or audit trails, potentially leading to data misuse.
assumptions: No additional context provided to confirm the specific validation process.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific validation process is fully documented in the context.

title: Data Integrity Violation
description: Process P1 may introduce or alter data integrity without proper checks, potentially leading to corrupted or inconsistent data.
assumptions: No additional context provided to confirm the specific integrity checks.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific integrity checks are fully documented in the context.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grading Service
description: The grading service (P2) writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory (DS3). If the service is not properly secured, an unauthorized user could access or modify these sensitive account records.

title: Data Modification by Grading Service
description: The grading service (P2) writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory (DS3). If the service is not properly secured, an unauthorized user could access or modify these sensitive account records.

title: Unauthorized Access to Account Directory
description: The account directory (DS3) receives account records and parent-child relationship links from the grading service (P2). If the directory is not properly secured, an unauthorized user could access or modify these sensitive account records.

title: Data Disclosure to External Entity
description: Process P2 (Assignment & Grading Service) shares full grade records, assignments, and account directory with external entity EE5 (Cloud Hosting Provider). This constitutes a data disclosure as the transfer of personal data across a boundary to a third party.
assumptions: The data transfer is intended and designed as part of the nightly backup and hosting replication process.

title: Data in Transit - Linking/Identification
description: Data-centric threat: The metadata associated with the data flow (e.g., source entity IDs, destination entity IDs, or other identifying information) may be used to link or identify the parties involved in the transfer, potentially compromising privacy.
assumptions: The metadata used to identify the parties is not strictly required for the backup process but is present in transit.

title: Data Processing/Storage by External Entity
description: External entity EE5 receives and processes the data. If the cloud provider stores or processes the data in a way that causes a threat (e.g., storing it in a way that allows re-identification or further processing), this is a data disclosure threat.
assumptions: The external entity's processing of the data is not strictly required for the backup process but is necessary for hosting.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The data store (DS2) shares grade records with the assignment & grading service (P2). If the service has access to the data, it can potentially access or modify the records, leading to unauthorized access.

title: Data Processing and Storage Risks
description: The assignment & grading service (P2) receives the grade records and processes them to build student, parent, and teacher views. This processing could lead to data being stored in a way that causes privacy threats.
